Own digest: Paper card. Question: Can medium-entropy alloying be used to improve the thermoelectric performance of GeTe-based alloys?. System: GeTe-based alloys with compositions such as Ge0.63Mn0.15Pb0.1Sb0.06Cd0.06Te. Processing: Medium-entropy alloying by co-alloying Mn, Pb, Sb, and Cd with GeTe. Test conditions: Temperature range of 300-873 K. Findings: A state-of-the-art zT of 2.1 at 873 K; High average zT ave value of 1.3 between 300 and 873 K; Record high Vickers hardness of 270; Lattice thermal conductivity of 0.30 W m−1 K−1 at 873 K; Seebeck coefficient of 197 µV K−1 at 300 K and 248 µV K−1 at 773 K. Mechanism: The authors propose that medium-entropy alloying suppresses the phase transition, reduces lattice thermal conductivity, and enhances the Seebeck coefficient through band convergence and increased band effective mass. Own digest: Paper card. Question: How do the phonon dynamics of the high-entropy alloy FeCoCrMnNi compare to those of glasses and complex metallic alloys (CMAs), and does it represent a unique class of materials?. System: Fe20Co20Cr20Mn20Ni20 (FeCoCrMnNi), a 5-element equiatomic FCC random solid solution. Processing: Polycrystalline samples produced by alloying high-purity elements in an inductively coupled high-frequency levitation furnace, slip-cast into a water-cooled copper mold, and annealed at 1200 °C for 48 h; single crystals grown via the Bridgman technique at 1340 °C with a solidification velocity of 50 mm/h under 200 mbar argon. Test conditions: Measurements performed at temperatures of 3, 15, 100, 200, and 300 K using inelastic neutron scattering (INS) and inelastic X-ray scattering (IXS); energy ranges up to 30 meV and wavevectors covering the Brillouin zone.
